title: Personal Portfolio Website
summary: A website I've built over the quarter to practice HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and now Eleventy.
overview: This started as a set of HTML pages for my web development class. Each assignment added something: responsive styles, theme switching, form validation, and a Web Component. For HW6, I moved the main portfolio into the Eleventy project I started in HW5.
process: I planned the original pages with wireframes and gave each page a specific purpose.
I built the pages in HTML and added shared styles for narrow screens and light and dark themes.
I moved repeated navigation and the footer into a shared Eleventy layout. The project index and detail pages now use the same JSON entries.
learning: The main change is how I maintain the site. I can edit the navigation once, or add one project entry, and rebuild instead of changing several HTML files by hand.
imageAlt: The earlier HTML version of my portfolio homepage
imageCaption: An earlier version of this portfolio, before the Eleventy migration.

title: Nachos Thread Exercise
summary: Operating systems coursework that helped me understand how multiple threads execute and switch between each other.
overview: In my operating systems class, I worked with Nachos to run a program involving multiple threads. The exercise connected the ideas from class to the order in which a program actually runs.
process: I ran the threaded program in the course's Nachos environment.
I followed how execution moved between threads instead of assuming one thread would finish first.
I used the exercise to connect thread behavior with what we were learning about operating systems.
learning: Working through the program helped me understand thread execution and context switching. It also gave me more practice using Linux for coursework. This page describes the exercise; course source code is not published here.

title: Horror Sound Design Project
summary: A music class project matching sound effects to a short horror clip in DaVinci Resolve.
overview: For a music class project, I added sound effects to a short horror clip. I used DaVinci Resolve to edit the audio and line up sounds with what was happening on screen.
process: I watched the clip to identify moments where sound could support the scene.
I edited the sound effects in DaVinci Resolve and matched their timing to the video.
I listened to the audio alongside the picture to hear how it changed the mood.
learning: This project made me pay more attention to sound in movies. One idea that stood out was the stinger: a short sound that emphasizes a sudden moment. A small timing change can make that moment feel different.
